title: The upper room (Mark 14:12–31)
hookLine: take, this is my body; this is my blood of the new testament

lines: THE DAY OF THE PASSOVER LAMBS.
FOLLOW THE MAN WITH THE WATER JAR.
cards: It's the first day of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lambs are sacrificed. Where should we get the meal ready, the disciples ask.
Jesus sends two of them into the city with odd directions: you'll meet a man carrying a jar of water. Follow him.
Ask the owner of the house he enters for the guest room, and he'll show you a large upper room, furnished and ready. It all happens just as he said. That evening Jesus arrives with the twelve.
Catholics trace every Mass back to what happens at this table.

teach.h: ONE OF YOU WILL BETRAY ME. IS IT I?
teach.b: First, the betrayal. While they're eating, Jesus says, in the Douay-Rheims: "one of you that eateth with me shall betray me." Heartbroken, one by one, they ask him: "Is it I?"
Nobody points at anyone else. Second, the bread. "And whilst they were eating, Jesus took bread; and blessing, broke, and gave to them, and said: Take ye. This is my body."

Took, blessed, broke, gave: almost the same four actions Mark used at the two feedings in the wilderness, and some readers hear those baskets echo here. Third, the cup. He gives thanks, and they all drink from it.
"This is my blood of the new testament, which shall be shed for many." Testament here means covenant, a binding promise.

teach.h: THE BLOOD OF THE NEW COVENANT.
teach.b: At Sinai, Moses sealed God's covenant with blood. Now Jesus speaks of his own. Fourth, what Catholics believe.
The Catholic Church teaches that at every Mass, when the priest speaks these words over bread and wine, they truly become the body and blood of Christ, while still looking like bread and wine.

teach.h: TAKE YE. THIS IS MY BODY.
teach.b: It calls this transubstantiation. Orthodox Christians also believe in a real change, and speak of it as a mystery; many Protestants understand the meal as a memorial or a spiritual presence.
And notice the first word over the bread: take. In Mark, the bread is given to be received.

Then they sing a hymn and walk out to the Mount of Olives, and Peter promises: "Although all shall be scandalized in thee, yet not I." Before the cock crows twice, Jesus tells him, you'll deny me three times.

how: At every Catholic Mass the priest repeats Jesus's words over the bread and wine at the consecration, and Catholics receive Communion believing it is truly the body and blood of Christ; the Last Supper is remembered especially on Holy Thursday.

games.q: you're at the table. Jesus says one of you will betray him. what do you ask?
games.why: they became sorrowful and asked, one by one, "Is it I?" each wondered about himself.

practice: Picture that room: low tables, lamplight, thirteen people close together, the smell of bread. Then picture your next meal, and one breath before it to remember this table.
If you pray, you can say grace, or simply thank you; if you don't, just notice the bread in your hands and who made it.

wordCard.voice: Transubstantiation. What Catholics believe happens at Mass when the priest repeats Jesus's words over bread and wine: they truly become his body and blood. Today's word.
